history.rationale: Initial baseline config with moderate depth and learning rate to establish a performance benchmark on this imbalanced dataset.
Testing shallower trees (depth 2) and higher min_child_weight to reduce overfitting on the rare positive class compared to trial 1.
Trial 2 showed strong gains with shallow depth; testing depth 3 with moderate learning rate to see if slight depth expansion captures interaction effects.
Testing a deeper tree regime (depth 6) to verify whether higher capacity degrades PR-AUC on this imbalanced dataset.
Trial 4 showed strong performance with high regularization and depth 6; testing depth 5 with slightly more trees to find the capacity sweet spot.
Trial 4 achieved 0.4949 with min_child_weight 6; increasing to 9 to further prevent noisy leaves on rare overtake events.
Exploring if fewer trees (90) and slightly lower min_child_weight (5) improve upon trial 4 by curbing late-stage overfitting.
Trial 7 improved to 0.4978 with 90 trees; testing 75 trees to pinpoint the exact peak before overfitting begins.
With 75 trees underfitting and 90 performing best, testing 100 trees to see if the peak lies between 90 and 120.
Testing higher colsample_bytree (0.7 vs 0.6) on top of the best trial 7 settings to evaluate feature sampling impact.
Colsample 0.6 outperformed 0.7; testing colsample 0.5 to see if stronger feature subsampling further improves generalization.
Testing subsample 0.8 versus 0.7 from trial 7 to determine if more data per tree reduces variance.
Subsample 0.8 deteriorated performance; testing subsample 0.6 to see if heavier instance bagging helps.
Testing min_child_weight 4 (vs 5 in trial 7) to see if allowing slightly smaller leaves enhances recall on rare positive cases.
Comparing min_child_weight 6 against 5 under the 90-tree configuration to check stability of the leaf size optimum.
Testing stronger L2 regularization (reg_lambda 7 vs 5) to see if shrinking leaf weights further boosts test-set ranking quality.
Testing slightly lower L2 regularization (reg_lambda 3 vs 5 and 7) to pinpoint the optimal leaf weight constraint.
Testing higher L1 penalty (reg_alpha 0.8 vs 0.5) to promote feature sparsity and reduce noise from less predictive features.
Testing lower L1 penalty (reg_alpha 0.2 vs 0.5) to see if milder sparsity preservation retains helpful subtle signals.
Testing max_depth 5 under the calibrated regularisation and tree count from trial 7 to isolate the true depth dependency.
Testing max_depth 4 with optimal regularisation to check if depth 5 was a sweet spot or if simpler trees reach higher scores.
Because depth 5 is less prone to overfitting than depth 6, testing 110 trees to see if more boosting rounds enhance learning.
Trial 22 showed 110 trees improved over 90; pushing to 130 trees to locate the upper bound of beneficial iterations.
Monotonic improvement from 90 -> 110 -> 130 trees suggests continuing upward to 150 trees to find the peak.
Since 130 was optimal and 150 overfitted, checking 125 trees to refine the exact peak in this interval.
Evaluating 135 trees to see if the peak sits slightly past 130 before falling off at 150.
Testing a slightly lower learning rate (0.03) with 140 trees to see if finer gradient steps achieve a smoother optimum.
Testing reg_lambda 6 (between 5 and 7) on the best overall configuration (trial 23) to see if slight additional shrinkage improves PR-AUC.
Re-evaluating min_child_weight 4 at the newly discovered optimal length of 130 trees to verify leaf-size sensitivity.
Testing a subtle fine-tuning of L1 regularisation (reg_alpha 0.4 vs 0.5) around the best trial 23 setup.

history.rationale: Initial baseline with moderate depth, learning rate, and subsampling to establish a solid benchmark.
Trial 1 achieved 0.482 with depth 4; testing shallow trees (depth 2) with higher min_child_weight to evaluate if simpler decision boundaries prevent overfitting on the 7% positive class.
Testing higher tree depth (depth 6) with stronger L2 regularization and lower learning rate to check if higher-order feature interactions boost PR-AUC beyond 0.482.
Trial 3 reached 0.4862 with depth 6; testing depth 5 with slightly more trees to see if intermediate depth provides better balance against overfitting.
Depth 6 (0.4862) outperformed depth 5 (0.4829); evaluating depth 7 with min_child_weight=5 to capture finer feature interactions while guarding leaf sample size.
Testing min_child_weight=2 on best model (Trial 3) to see if allowing smaller leaves captures high-precision positive clusters.
Since min_child_weight=2 degraded performance, testing min_child_weight=6 to check if larger leaf regularization improves generalization.
Trial 7 showed significant improvement with min_child_weight=6 (0.4903); testing min_child_weight=8 to see if stronger minimum leaf sample weight yields further gains.
min_child_weight=6 scored 0.4903 and 8 scored 0.4848; testing 7 to check whether the optimal leaf weight is slightly above 6.
Comparing min_child_weight=5 against 6 (0.4903) and 4 (0.4862) to locate the exact optimum between 4 and 6.
Testing n_estimators=250 with best params (Trial 10, 0.4910) to see if additional boosting iterations improve calibration.
Since 250 estimators overfit (0.4864 vs 0.4910 at 200), testing 160 estimators to find whether the peak is before 200.
Lowering learning rate to 0.02 with 260 estimators to test if finer shrinkage achieves better generalization than lr=0.03 at 200.
Evaluating lr=0.04 with 160 estimators to see if slightly faster learning with fewer trees preserves peak validation PR-AUC.
Evaluating colsample_bytree=0.6 with best settings (Trial 10) to see if more feature sub-sampling reduces tree correlation.
Testing colsample_bytree=0.8 against 0.7 to see if more feature availability per tree improves precision-recall trade-offs.
Since 0.7 yielded 0.4910 and 0.8 yielded 0.4885, testing intermediate colsample_bytree=0.75.
Testing higher subsample=0.85 from 0.75 to see if larger training sample per tree stabilizes PR-AUC.
Subsample 0.85 reduced performance; testing subsample=0.65 to see if stronger instance sub-sampling prevents overfitting.
Evaluating subsample=0.80 between 0.75 (0.4910) and 0.85 (0.4872) to refine the instance subsample rate.
Checking subsample=0.70 to see if slightly tighter subsampling outperforms 0.75 (0.4910).
Testing lower reg_lambda=3.0 (vs 5.0) to see if easing L2 shrinkage allows slightly more expressive leaf weights.
Since reg_lambda=3 degraded score, testing reg_lambda=7.0 to see if stronger L2 shrinkage pushes PR-AUC higher.
Testing reg_lambda=5.5 between 5.0 and 7.0 to verify if peak is slightly higher than 5.0.
Evaluating reg_alpha=0.1 (vs 0.2) to determine if lighter L1 sparsity regularization improves PR-AUC.
Since reg_alpha=0.1 degraded performance relative to 0.2, testing reg_alpha=0.3 to see if stronger L1 regularization boosts sparsity and generalization.
Fine-tuning n_estimators around the 200 peak (0.4910) by testing 210 iterations.
Since 210 estimators scored 0.4895 vs 0.4910 at 200, testing 190 to check if the peak lies slightly below 200.
Trial 28 at 190 estimators reached 0.4930; testing 180 estimators to explore further in the direction of fewer trees.
With 180 yielding 0.4920 and 190 yielding 0.4930, evaluating 188 estimators to pinpoint the optimal stopping point.

history.rationale: Initial baseline with moderate depth and standard regularization to anchor the search space.
Trial 1 achieved 0.4857 with depth 4; testing shallower depth (3) with higher min_child_weight and more regularisation to prevent overfitting on the 7% minority class.
Trial 2 improved over Trial 1 by lowering depth to 3; testing depth 2 to see if strong simplification further improves PR-AUC or underfits.

Trial 2 (depth 3, 0.4968) beat Trial 1 (depth 4, 0.4857) and Trial 3 (depth 2, 0.4889); testing depth 4 with stronger regularisation and min_child_weight to see if depth 4 can outperform depth 3 with better control.
Trial 2 established depth 3 as the strongest candidate (0.4968); testing whether higher min_child_weight (7 vs 5) further reduces noise in sparse positive leaf nodes.
Comparing min_child_weight 5 (0.4968) and 7 (0.4963), testing min_child_weight 4 to locate the exact optimum between 3 and 5.
Trial 6 improved to 0.4975 with min_child_weight 4; testing min_child_weight 3 to test the lower boundary on depth 3.
Trial 7 edged higher with min_child_weight 3 (0.4975); testing min_child_weight 2 to see if lower restriction provides further benefit.
Trial 8 improved to 0.4977 with min_child_weight 2; testing min_child_weight 1 to check the lower bound.
Holding optimal depth 3 and min_child_weight 2 from Trial 8, testing smaller learning rate (0.02) with proportionately more trees (375) for finer gradient steps.
Trial 10 saw big gains at lr=0.02 with 375 trees (0.4990); testing if more trees (450) further refines predictions without overfitting.
Since 450 trees in Trial 11 overfit compared to 375 trees in Trial 10, testing 325 trees to locate the peak between 250 and 375.
Trial 12 (325 trees, 0.4995) beat Trial 10 (375 trees, 0.4990); testing 300 trees to check if optimal tree count is closer to 300.
Progression from 375 to 325 to 300 monotonically improved val_pr_auc to 0.4997; testing 275 trees to find the peak.
Trial 14 reached 0.5003 at 275 trees; testing 250 trees at lr=0.02 to determine if the optimum is even lower.
Trial 15 jumped to 0.5014 at 250 trees; testing 225 trees to check whether the optimal capacity is around 225.
Val PR-AUC climbed to 0.5027 at 225 trees; testing 200 trees to see if reduction continues improving performance.
With 200 trees (0.5007) and 250 trees (0.5014) bracketing 225 trees (0.5027), testing 235 trees to pinpoint the peak.
Testing 215 trees to see if the peak lies between 200 and 225.
Holding best tree structure from Trial 16, testing subsample 0.8 vs 0.7 to evaluate data variance control.
Subsample 0.8 (0.5023) scored below 0.7 (0.5027); testing subsample 0.6 to see if more aggressive row bagging helps minority class focus.
Subsample 0.7 is verified as best; testing colsample_bytree 0.8 to see if more feature coverage per tree improves representation.
colsample_bytree 0.8 underperformed 0.7; testing colsample_bytree 0.6 to see if greater feature subsampling prevents overfitting.
With subsample and colsample optimised at 0.7, testing stronger L2 regularization (reg_lambda=5.0 vs 3.0) to penalize large leaf weights.
reg_lambda=5 (0.5007) was too strong compared to 3 (0.5027); testing reg_lambda=2.0 to see if slightly looser L2 improves predictions.
reg_lambda=3 (0.5027) beat both 2 (0.5023) and 5 (0.5007); testing reg_lambda=3.5 to fine-tune around 3.
reg_lambda=3.5 improved over 3.0 to 0.5028; testing reg_lambda=4.0 to see if the peak is near 4.0.
reg_lambda=4 (0.5032) beat 3.5 (0.5028) while 5.0 (0.5007) dropped; testing reg_lambda=4.5 to bracket the exact peak.
With reg_lambda=4.0 confirmed optimal (0.5032), testing lower L1 penalty (reg_alpha=0.05 vs 0.1) to see if slight feature sparsity relaxation helps.
reg_alpha=0.05 underperformed 0.10 (0.5032); testing reg_alpha=0.15 to see if slightly stronger L1 regularization improves minority signal filtering.
